# crosswork_srte_policies (Resource)

This resource can manage an SR-TE policy. Create and update wait until the devices named in `head_end` are ready in Crosswork, as set by the `device_ready_mode` and `device_ready_timeout` arguments of the provider configuration.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "crosswork_srte_policies" "example" {
  name                                       = "cwtest-policy"
  head_end                                   = "build-router-1"
  tail_end                                   = "192.0.2.61"
  color                                      = 999
  binding_sid                                = 24001
  bandwidth                                  = 1000
  source_address                             = "192.0.2.1"
  delay_measurement_profile                  = "delay-profile-1"
  delay_measurement_logging_delay_exceeded   = true
  performance_measurement_reverse_path_label = 2000
  auto_route_metric_relative                 = -5
  auto_route_include_prefixes = [
    {
      prefix_address = "10.250.0.0/16"
    }
  ]
  auto_route_force_sr_include = true
  auto_route_forward_class    = 2
  paths = [
    {
      preference = 100
      explicit_sid_lists = [
        {
          name   = "cwtest-sid-list"
          weight = 10
        }
      ]
      explicit_affinity_rules = [
        {
          action = "include-any"
          colors = ["red"]
        }
      ]
      explicit_segments_sid_algorithm = 128
      explicit_disjoint_path_type     = "link"
      explicit_disjoint_path_group_id = 1
      explicit_disjoint_path_sub_id   = 1
    }
  ]
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `color` (Number) Color of the policy. The head end holds one policy for a color and a tail end.
  - Range: `1`-`4294967295`
- `head_end` (String) Head end of the policy, the name of a device in the Crosswork inventory that is onboarded to NSO. A policy has exactly one head end.
- `name` (String) Policy name. Letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`; a space or a slash is refused.
- `paths` (Attributes List) Candidate paths of the policy, at least one. A path is explicit (`explicit_*`) or dynamic (`dynamic_*`), not both. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--paths))
- `tail_end` (String) Tail end of the policy, an IP address. An IPv6 address needs SRv6 and SRv6 needs an IPv6 address.

### Optional

- `auto_route_force_sr_include` (Boolean) Steer the prefixes into the policy even when the router prefers another next hop. Set to `true` or leave unset.
- `auto_route_forward_class` (Number) Forward class of the steered traffic
  - Range: `0`-`7`
- `auto_route_include_prefixes` (Attributes Set) IPv4 prefixes that the policy steers. Without a prefix the device includes all of them. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--auto_route_include_prefixes))
- `auto_route_metric_constant` (Number) Constant auto-route metric. Use this or the relative metric.
  - Range: `1`-`2147483647`
- `auto_route_metric_relative` (Number) Relative auto-route metric. Use this or the constant metric.
  - Range: `-10`-`10`
- `bandwidth` (Number) Requested bandwidth in kbps. Not supported together with SRv6.
  - Range: `1`-`4294967295`
- `binding_sid` (Number) MPLS binding SID of the policy
  - Range: `16`-`1048575`
- `delay_measurement_logging_delay_exceeded` (Boolean) Log when the delay is exceeded. Set to `true` or leave unset.
- `delay_measurement_profile` (String) Delay measurement profile of the head end. Not `default`; leave it unset for the default profile. Use this or liveness detection.
- `instance` (String) Select an instance of the provider configuration by its name. Leave it unset to use the default instance.
- `liveness_detection_backup` (String) Backup liveness detection profile. Needs a profile.
- `liveness_detection_invalidation_action` (String) Action when the liveness session invalidates the path
  - Choices: `down`, `none`
- `liveness_detection_logging_session_state_change` (Boolean) Log a change of the liveness session state. Set to `true` or leave unset.
- `liveness_detection_profile` (String) Liveness detection profile. Not `default`. Use this or delay measurement.
- `performance_measurement_reverse_path_label` (Number) Reverse path label of the performance measurement
  - Range: `16`-`1048575`
- `source_address` (String) Source address of the policy. It has the address family of the tail end.
- `srv6_locator_behavior` (String) SRv6 behavior of the locator
  - Choices: `ub6-insert-reduced`
- `srv6_locator_binding_sid_type` (String) SRv6 binding SID type
  - Choices: `srv6-dynamic`
- `srv6_locator_name` (String) SRv6 locator name. Setting any SRv6 attribute turns on SRv6 for the policy

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The id of the object

<a id="nestedatt--paths"></a>
### Nested Schema for `paths`

Required:

- `preference` (Number) Preference of the path, unique in the policy
  - Range: `1`-`65535`

Optional:

- `dynamic_affinity_rules` (Attributes List) Affinity rules of a dynamic path (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--paths--dynamic_affinity_rules))
- `dynamic_disjoint_path_group_id` (Number) Disjoint group id of a dynamic path. Required with the type.
  - Range: `1`-`65535`
- `dynamic_disjoint_path_sub_id` (Number) Disjoint sub group id of a dynamic path
  - Range: `1`-`65535`
- `dynamic_disjoint_path_type` (String) Disjointness type of a dynamic path. With the group id it makes the paths of the group disjoint.
  - Choices: `link`, `node`, `srlg`, `srlg-node`
- `dynamic_metric_margin_absolute` (Number) Absolute metric margin of a dynamic path. Use this or the relative margin.
  - Range: `0`-`2147483647`
- `dynamic_metric_margin_relative` (Number) Relative metric margin of a dynamic path in percent. Use this or the absolute margin.
  - Range: `0`-`2147483647`
- `dynamic_metric_type` (String) Metric type of the path computation of a dynamic path
  - Choices: `hopcount`, `igp`, `latency`, `te`
- `dynamic_pce` (Boolean) Delegate the path computation to the PCE. Set to `true` or leave unset.
- `dynamic_segments_sid_algorithm` (Number) SID algorithm constraint of a dynamic path
  - Range: `128`-`255`
- `dynamic_sid_limit` (Number) Maximum number of SIDs of a dynamic path.
  - Range: `1`-`255`
- `explicit_affinity_rules` (Attributes List) Affinity rules of an explicit path (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--paths--explicit_affinity_rules))
- `explicit_disjoint_path_group_id` (Number) Disjoint group id of an explicit path. Required with the type.
  - Range: `1`-`65535`
- `explicit_disjoint_path_sub_id` (Number) Disjoint sub group id of an explicit path
  - Range: `1`-`65535`
- `explicit_disjoint_path_type` (String) Disjointness type of an explicit path. With the group id it makes the paths of the group disjoint.
  - Choices: `link`, `node`, `srlg`, `srlg-node`
- `explicit_segments_sid_algorithm` (Number) SID algorithm constraint of an explicit path
  - Range: `128`-`255`
- `explicit_sid_lists` (Attributes List) SID lists of an explicit path, with their weights. At least one for an explicit path. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--paths--explicit_sid_lists))

<a id="nestedatt--paths--dynamic_affinity_rules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `paths.dynamic_affinity_rules`

Required:

- `action` (String) Rule action
  - Choices: `exclude-any`, `include-all`, `include-any`

Optional:

- `colors` (Set of String) Names of the affinity colors of the rule. NSO returns them sorted.


<a id="nestedatt--paths--explicit_affinity_rules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `paths.explicit_affinity_rules`

Required:

- `action` (String) Rule action
  - Choices: `exclude-any`, `include-all`, `include-any`

Optional:

- `colors` (Set of String) Names of the affinity colors of the rule. NSO returns them sorted.


<a id="nestedatt--paths--explicit_sid_lists"></a>
### Nested Schema for `paths.explicit_sid_lists`

Required:

- `name` (String) Name of a SID list

Optional:

- `weight` (Number) Weight of the SID list when the path has several
  - Range: `1`-`4294967295`



<a id="nestedatt--auto_route_include_prefixes"></a>
### Nested Schema for `auto_route_include_prefixes`

Required:

- `prefix_address` (String) IPv4 prefix with its length

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import crosswork_srte_policies.example "<name>"
```
